rule: a local inside a function that is bound to a table constructor (`local T = {}` or `local T = { ... }`) and never reassigned in its scope: `mod.T#f`. Every such table of that name in a file shares the ID, as overloads do. Calls `T.f()` and `T:f()` on such a table resolve to that ID (high when defined).
source: KNOWN_GAP: forward-declared locals and function-local tables are under-resolved
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. Both functions bind a local `T` to a table constructor (`{}` in build, `{ size = 0 }` in other) and never reassign it, so `function T.step` (build), `T.finish = function` (build) and `function T:step` (other) are `builder.T#step` / `builder.T#finish`; the two `step` definitions share one ID ('as overloads do'). The enclosing function is not part of the ID (`mod.T#f`). `self.size` is field access.
